title: Duke Ellington's Breaking in a Pair of Shoes
summary: Ellington gave Chuck and Chuckles the song Breaking in a Pair of Shoes; they filled in for Tip, Tap and Toe on an Ellington tour, with one singing while the other danced.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Oh, my goodness. Well, if there's been some people writing songs, they all come by Duke Ellington especially. He composed a song, him and one of his colleagues, they composed a song called, "Breaking in A Pair of Shoes". And he gave that to Chuck and Chuckles as a present, you see. We pinch hitted one time for the great team of Tip, Tap and Toe, see, on a Duke Ellington itinerary, which was a chartered tour here in the United States.
Well, it was something. All dressed up, high hat and everything. All dressed up, looking good and (unintelligible). he can sing. (Singing), "There he goes. Here am I, breaking in a pair of shoes."

No, sir. Looley, here, I sings, you know, but I don't sing without an instrument. And as you know, well you do have a radio somewhere. Well, I'll get a song to sing for you. Because I used to try to sing ballads, you see. And after that I learned a different style of doing a song, which is not considered singing, called satire, you see. Like a poet would explain in a poem, you see. It was like that.
Well, what do you -- could you demonstrate what that different style of singing was for you?
Well, I never did -- when was it? I
You were dancing while you were singing?

No. See, we had -- my partner sang the song. He sang and I danced. And then I sang while he danced. Like that, see? It was a separation dance, you know. Like I say, each one of them -- I think Mr. Bubbles has got that song, that music, the words to it, or this lady down at 57th Street, George Gershwin's sister. I think I can get it from her. See, once they pass, you see these people died, you see. I try to discontinue remembering some of the things that we were mostly attached to, you see. Because I was kind of hurt when they passed. I wouldn't want to try to discontinue, you know, remembering them, certain kinds of conditions.
